questions.question: In traffic, how much stopping distance do motorcycles need compared to cars?

options.text: Much less distance than cars
Less distance than cars
The same distance as cars
More distance than cars

questions.correctAnswerText: The same distance as cars
questions.explanation: Motorcycles need the same stopping distance as cars.

questions.question: If you are stopped for a traffic violation while wearing a helmet and you are 18 or older, what happens?

options.text: You will not get a ticket
You get extra time to pay the fine
$8 of the fine will be waived
The ticket won't appear on your driving record

questions.correctAnswerText: $8 of the fine will be waived
questions.explanation: In Utah, riders 18 and older are not required to wear helmets. However, if you wear one and get a traffic ticket, $8 of the fine is waived to encourage helmet use.

questions.question: When riding with a passenger, which instruction should you NOT give them?

options.text: Get on after the engine starts
Sit as far forward as possible without crowding you
Hold firmly onto your waist, hips, or belt
Talk whenever they want

questions.correctAnswerText: Talk whenever they want
questions.explanation: Passengers should avoid talking or moving during the ride. You need to focus on riding. Passengers should only get on after the engine starts, sit forward without crowding you, and hold firmly to your waist, hips, or belt.

questions.question: Why should you NOT move to the far side of your lane when being passed?

options.text: It discourages the passing driver from cutting in too early
It encourages the passing driver to cut in too early
It makes the passing driver pass more quickly
It encourages other drivers to pass you

questions.correctAnswerText: It encourages the passing driver to cut in too early
questions.explanation: Moving to the far side of your lane is dangerous. It may encourage the passing driver to return to your lane before it is safe. Stay in the center of your lane when being passed.

questions.question: If your front wheel starts to skid, what should you do?

options.text: Keep the front brake engaged and ride out the skid
Keep the front brake engaged and release the rear brake
Release and re-engage the front brake right away
Release the front brake and press harder on the rear brake

questions.correctAnswerText: Release and re-engage the front brake right away
questions.explanation: If your front wheel locks while braking, release the front brake completely right away. Then apply it again smoothly.

questions.question: Which vest or jacket color helps you be seen the best?

options.text: Red
Black
Silver
Blue

questions.correctAnswerText: Red
questions.explanation: Wear bright colors to be seen. Red, orange, yellow, and green are best. Avoid dark or dull colors.

questions.question: When preparing to pass another rider on the left, where should you position your motorcycle?

options.text: In the right part of the lane to be seen in their mirror
In the left part of the lane to see better
In the center of the lane to be seen in their mirror
Weave in your lane to get attention

questions.correctAnswerText: In the left part of the lane to see better
questions.explanation: Ride in the left part of your lane to see ahead better and be more visible. Check your mirrors and look over your shoulder before passing.

questions.question: How should you load cargo on a motorcycle?

options.text: Put heavier items in front of the tank bag
Put lighter items near the front
Try to avoid placing items over the rear axle
Place items behind the rear axle

questions.correctAnswerText: Put heavier items in front of the tank bag
questions.explanation: Load heavier items in front of the tank bag. Place the load over or in front of the rear axle. Putting the load behind the rear axle makes it harder to control your motorcycle.

questions.question: If you cannot avoid hitting an object in the road, what should you do?

options.text: Speed up before contact
Slow down before contact
Lean the motorcycle
Stay seated on the motorcycle

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down before contact
questions.explanation: Slow down as much as you can before hitting the object. Try to hit it at a 90-degree angle. Keep your motorcycle upright, rise slightly off your seat, and roll the throttle slightly to lighten the front end just before impact.

questions.question: Which is a poor reason to use your horn?

options.text: A driver next to you is following the car ahead too closely
A parked car has someone in the driver's seat
You want people to look at your motorcycle
You are passing a pedestrian in the street

questions.correctAnswerText: You want people to look at your motorcycle
questions.explanation: Use your horn to alert drivers or pedestrians who might move into your path. Sound it before passing a car, if someone is in a parked car's driver seat, or if you see a pedestrian or bicyclist in the street. Do not use it just to get attention.

questions.question: When your motorcycle's weight shifts forward while braking, you:

options.text: Can apply the front brake harder.
Should use less pressure on the front brake.
Can apply the rear brake harder.
Lose traction.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can apply the front brake harder.
questions.explanation: When your weight shifts forward while braking, the front wheel gets more grip. This means you can use more pressure on the front brake.

questions.question: If your throttle gets stuck, you should:

options.text: Jump off the motorcycle.
Apply the brakes.
Twist the throttle back and forth several times.
Not try to twist the throttle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Twist the throttle back and forth several times.
questions.explanation: If your throttle is stuck, try twisting it back and forth several times to free it. If that does not work, use the engine cut-off switch and pull in the clutch right away.

questions.question: Helmets are:

options.text: Required for all riders under 18 years old.
Required for all riders under 21 years old.
Required only for riders who have had their license for less than two years.
Never required.

questions.correctAnswerText: Required for all riders under 18 years old.
questions.explanation: In Utah, all motorcycle riders and passengers under 18 must wear a helmet. Helmets are strongly recommended for all riders, regardless of age.

questions.question: Who should set the pace when riding in a group?

options.text: The leader
The riders just behind the leader
The last rider
The oldest rider

questions.correctAnswerText: The last rider
questions.explanation: The last rider in a group should set the pace. This makes sure no one gets left behind.

questions.question: Without a helmet, a rider is ________ more likely to suffer a serious head injury in a crash.

options.text: Three times
Four times
Five times
Six times

questions.correctAnswerText: Five times
questions.explanation: Riders without helmets are five times more likely to get a serious head injury in a crash.

questions.question: What type of sign is yellow with black lettering or symbols?

options.text: Warning
Service
Regulatory
Speed limit

questions.correctAnswerText: Warning
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They alert drivers to upcoming road conditions.

questions.question: When stopping, the best technique is to:

options.text: Grab at the front brake lever.
Keep your knees against the gas tank and look ahead.
Apply increasing pressure to the rear brake.
Use only the front brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your knees against the gas tank and look ahead.
questions.explanation: Apply the brakes smoothly and firmly. As your weight shifts forward, the front wheel gets more grip. You can then use more front brake pressure while using less rear brake pressure. Keep your knees on the gas tank and look ahead to stay in a straight line.

questions.question: Which factor does NOT affect a person's blood alcohol content (BAC)?

options.text: The amount of alcohol consumed
Body weight
How quickly the alcohol was consumed
How often a person drinks alcohol

questions.correctAnswerText: How often a person drinks alcohol
questions.explanation: The three main factors that affect BAC are the amount of alcohol consumed, how fast it was consumed, and body weight. Sex, physical condition, and food intake can also have an effect.

questions.question: Maximum straight-line braking is done by:

options.text: Using the rear brake only.
Using the front brake only.
Using both brakes.
Using the rear brake while downshifting.

questions.correctAnswerText: Using both brakes.
questions.explanation: Maximum braking power comes from using both the front and rear brakes together without locking either wheel. Use both brakes every time you slow down or stop.

questions.question: What does this hand signal mean?

options.text: Follow me
Slow down
Speed up
Exit

questions.correctAnswerText: Follow me
questions.explanation: Hand signals help riders communicate in a group. This signal means "follow me."

questions.question: At night, what is the minimum following distance a motorcyclist should keep?

options.text: Two seconds.
Three seconds.
Four seconds.
Five seconds.

questions.correctAnswerText: Three seconds.
questions.explanation: At night, it is harder to see and judge distances. You need at least three seconds of distance between you and the vehicle ahead. This extra space gives you time to notice when the vehicle stops and time to slow down or stop safely.

questions.question: When crossing angled railroad tracks, what is the safest way to approach them?

options.text: By proceeding straight within your lane.
At a 45-degree angle.
At a 90-degree angle.
At a fast speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: By proceeding straight within your lane.
questions.explanation: Go straight ahead in your lane when crossing angled railroad tracks. Turning to hit the tracks at a right angle is dangerous because it can push you into another lane.

questions.question: When riding a three-wheeled motorcycle through a curve, what should you do?

options.text: Stay in the center of the lane.
Stay on the outside of the lane.
Change your path as needed.
Use the shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change your path as needed.
questions.explanation: A three-wheeled motorcycle handles curves differently than a two-wheeled motorcycle. The best path through a curve may not follow the curve exactly. You may need to move from the outside of the curve to the inside before straightening out.

questions.question: When being passed, why should you not move to the far side of your lane?

options.text: The passing vehicle may re-enter your lane too early.
You may prevent another vehicle from passing you.
The portion of the lane nearest the passing vehicle is better.
You are more likely to experience a wind blast from the passing vehicle on the far side of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: The passing vehicle may re-enter your lane too early.
questions.explanation: When being passed, stay on the side of your lane closest to the passing vehicle. Moving to the far side may encourage the other driver to return to your lane before it is safe to do so.

questions.question: When you must both brake and swerve to avoid a hazard, what should you do?

options.text: Perform one action, then the other.
Perform both actions at the same time and apply extra braking pressure.
Perform both actions at the same time, but mainly focus on swerving.
Not perform either action.

questions.correctAnswerText: Perform one action, then the other.
questions.explanation: Do not brake and swerve at the same time because you need good traction to swerve safely. Instead, do one action first, then the other.
